author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical Customer Success & Support playbook for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It consolidates the onboarding checklist, integration guide, escalation playbook, known issues and workarounds, and Health Check / QBR cadence for production customers. Intended audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Support Engineers (L2/L3), Solutions Engineers, and Platform/Infra owners.

Goals
- Accelerate time-to-value for enterprise customers (target: production integration within 6-8 weeks).
- Provide deterministic escalation paths with measurable SLAs.
- Standardize integration and handoff steps for Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Ensure QBRs focus on reliability, cost, and roadmap alignment.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) customers.
- Does not replace team-specific runbooks located in eng-sre or eng-serving-runtime; instead it references them for operational details.

Ownership and Roles
- CSM (primary owner): overall customer relationship, onboarding schedule, QBRs.
- Solutions Engineer: API/SDK, integration support, test harness setup.
- Support L2: triage customer-reported issues and perform initial remediation.
- Support L3 / Eng on-call: deep debugging, bug fixes, infra escalations.
- Product/Platform Owner: prioritize rollout/backfill for product-impacting issues.

Contact Matrix
- Primary CSM: assigned per account (CS portal).
- Support Slack channel: #support-enterprise (monitoring during onboarding).
- Pager rotation: eng-oncall@redwood.com (SEV1/2 after escalation).

SLOs and Response Targets
- Customer Success / Support targets for enterprise onboarding phase:
  - P1 (Service down / severe data loss): initial response within 1 hour, mitigation plan in 4 hours, full resolution target 72 hours (or agreed SLA).
  - P2 (Partial outage / degraded performance): initial response within 4 hours, workaround/mitigation in 24 hours, resolution target 7 days.
  - P3 (Feature requests / integrations): response in 48 hours, roadmap alignment in next QBR or roadmap sync.
- Internal SLO: onboarding playbooks and integration guides updated within 2 business days after product or infra changes.

Onboarding Checklist (Milestone-driven)
1) Discovery (Week 0-1)
   - Review customer compliance and data residency requirements. Confirm whether Hosted / Dedicated / Private is required.
   - Collect integration contacts, expected traffic profile (rps, qps, token distribution), and peak window times.
   - Share onboarding timeline and required artifacts checklist.

2) Access & Security (Week 1-2)
   - Provision API keys and scoped tokens. For Private deployments, coordinate KMS/HSM and network peering.
   - Perform RBAC setup in Console for customer technical contacts.
   - Verify audit-logging is enabled for production (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging).

3) Integration & Sandbox Testing (Week 2-4)
   - Provide sample prompts and prompt-sets used for evals.
   - Run end-to-end integration tests: auth, rate limits, streaming, function calling.
   - Validate model selection and quantization profile. Reference quantization guide: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles.

4) Performance Tuning & Capacity Planning (Week 3-6)
   - Use customer's traffic profile to recommend Dedicated pool sizing or autoscaling policies. Typical config examples:

   - Recommended Dedicated pool for chat-heavy workloads: 4 x A100-80GB + burst policy 2x for peak hours.
   - Autoscale policy example: min_replicas: 2, target_rps_per_replica: 80, cooldown: 300s.

   - Run load tests against staging endpoints (scripts provided by SE team). Collect latency p50/p95/p99 and token cost estimates.

5) Security Review & Compliance (Week 4-6)
   - Complete compliance questionnaire and PO/contract items.
   - For Private deployments, validate network ACLs, KMS integration, and data retention settings.

6) Go-live & Post-Launch (Week 6-8)
   - Confirm canary rollout policy: 5% traffic for 24 hours, monitor latency and error rate.
   - Schedule 30/60/90 day health checks and QBR. Close onboarding checklist when key integration flows pass smoke tests.

Integration Guide (Key Steps & Examples)
- API endpoints and common flows:
  - Authentication: Bearer API Key via Authorization header.
  - Generation: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  - Embeddings: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

- Example curl to stream logs and verify streaming endpoint:
  - curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-small-chat", "input":"Hello"}'

- Common troubleshooting commands (support engineers):
  - Fetch recent request logs (kibana query): service:redwood-api AND customer_id:<ID> AND @timestamp:>=now-1h
  - Check routing service health (kubernetes): kubectl -n routing get pods -l app=routing-service
  - Tail model server logs: kubectl -n models logs -l app=model-server --since=2h

- Integration test checklist:
  - Auth valid for server-to-server and front-end use.
  - Streaming and chunking tested with representative payloads.
  - Rate limit behavior verified: soft-limit warnings and enforced bursts.

Escalation Playbook (Step-by-step)
- Priority determination:
  1. Confirm impact (number of customers affected, business impact, data integrity).
  2. Assign a severity (P1/P2/P3) and notify appropriate stakeholders.

- Escalation flow (P1 example):
  1. Immediately notify on-call engineer via PagerDuty and post to #incident-respond.
  2. CSM notifies customer and schedules immediate bridge (Zoom) if requested.
  3. L2 performs triage using standard runbooks. If not resolved in 30 minutes, escalate to L3 and Eng on-call.
  4. Product owner joins bridge if issue requires release or rollback decision.
  5. Post-resolution: write an incident summary and schedule a postmortem within 3 business days.

- Communication templates (use these for consistent customer updates):
  - Acknowledge: \"We received your report and have opened incident <INC-####>. Our initial response target is 1 hour.\"
  - Status update: \"INC-#### update: Root cause identified (routing-service TX queue), mitigation in progress (deploy hotfix). ETA 2 hours.\"
  - Resolution: \"INC-#### resolved: Cause and actions taken. Postmortem scheduled for <date>.\"

Known Issues & Workarounds
- Issue: Intermittent 502s from dedicated-gpu-pool during peak inference bursts.
  - Symptom: p95 latency spikes and increased 502 rates between 18:00-20:00 UTC.
  - Workaround: Temporarily increase burst capacity and enable prefix caching for high-volume clients. Command example to increase burst config:
    - rwdctl capacity update --pool dedicated-123 --burst-multiplier 2
  - Permanent fix: Patch scheduled in next runtime release (refer to eng-serving-runtime/release-notes).

- Issue: Streaming responses truncated when using custom proxy with chunk-size < 8KB.
  - Symptom: Clients report missing final tokens.
  - Workaround: Recommend proxy keepalive and minimum chunk-size 16KB; add buffering on proxy layer.
  - Reference: integration checklist includes proxy compatibility tests.

- Issue: Embeddings mismatch post-quantization for some models.
  - Symptom: Small semantic drift observed on low-recall queries after quantization.
  - Workaround: Use quantization profile qv2-medium for embeddings-sensitive workloads or fall back to full-precision for vector indexing jobs.

Support Process & Ticketing
- Ticketing flow:
  1. Customer opens a ticket via Support Portal or email to support@redwood.ai.
  2. Support L1 reviews and triages the request within 4 hours.
  3. If the issue requires technical investigation, escalate to L2 and assign to a CSM/Solutions Engineer.
  4. For product bugs, create an internal bug in the engineering tracker with severity and customer impact.

- Ticket fields and required information:
  - Customer ID, account tier, environment (staging/prod), timestamps, example request payloads, correlation IDs/trace IDs.

Health Checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs)
- Health check cadence: 30/60/90 day check-ins during onboarding, then monthly health checks for the first 6 months post-go-live.
- Health check checklist:
  - Latency & error rate trends (p50/p95/p99, 30-day window).
  - Capacity utilization and cost-per-token estimates.
  - Security posture: audit-logging, RBAC, KMS status.
  - Integration stability: failure rates and retry behavior.

- QBR agenda (recommended 60-90 minutes):
  1. Executive summary & key metrics (5-10 min).
  2. Reliability and incidents since last QBR (10-15 min).
  3. Usage & cost breakdown with recommendations (15-20 min).
  4. Product roadmap and upcoming infra changes (15 min).
  5. Open action items and timeline (10-15 min).

- QBR deliverables:
  - Slide deck with metrics, recommended configuration changes, and action owners.
  - Updated roadmap and next steps.
  - Health check artifact stored in customer folder: s3://redwood-enterprise-onboarding/<customer-id>/qbr/<date>.pdf

Reporting and Dashboards
- Use Console dashboards to produce customer-facing reports: per-route latency, token cost, model usage, and error breakdown.
- Pre-built dashboard templates exist under eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts and can be cloned per customer.

Postmortems and Continuous Improvement
- All P1 incidents require a postmortem within 3 business days. Postmortems must include: timeline, root cause, remediation, and action owners.
- Maintain a running retrospective of common onboarding blockers and feed into product backlog for friction reduction.
